newsitem.title: USA: Grain group's China forecast "rosy" - USDA analyst.
newsitem.headline: Grain group's China forecast "rosy" - USDA analyst.

text.p: A U.S. Agriculture Department analyst said a trade group's recent prediction that China would import huge quantities of feed grains in the coming decade was "a little bit rosy."

In an interview with USDA radio, USDA China specialist Frederick Crook said China was trying to push a policy of grain self-sufficiency. The country had a record corn crop and might end up a net exporter of corn this season, he said.
In the longer term, Crook said, "There will be a growing demand for feed grains and oilseed meals in the future. China's livestock production is going to expand."
He said China could import 12 million tonnes of corn a year by 2005 and the United States would probably be the main supplier.

The U.S. Feed Grains Council earlier this week forecast that China would import a net 1.5 million tonnes of feed grain in the current marketing year, leaping to 4.255 million tonnes in 1997/98 and 23.5 million tonnes in 2005, an annual average annual growth of 36 percent over the next nine years.
